claims.content: To unlock a customer's "Review Status" account so that the customer can bid again after nonpayment.

goal.raw_text: To unlock a customer's "Review Status" account so that the customer can bid again after nonpayment.

claims.content: Customer Service Representative
The customer's account is in "Review Status" because the system automatically locked it after a PayPal or Amazon Payments customer allowed their order(s) to expire.
The customer's order(s) were automatically cancelled after 7 days (168 hours).
The customer has had orders cancelled and has not paid up to three times.
The customer has contacted the call center.
If the customer is subject to the escalation policy, the customer has updated their account with a credit card.
A customer whose account is in Review Status contacts the call center after nonpayment.

trigger.raw_text: A customer whose account is in Review Status contacts the call center after nonpayment.

claims.content: The Customer Service Representative accesses the Customer History page to troubleshoot the customer's account issue.
The Customer Service Representative searches for the customer by customer e-mail address, phone number, or customer name.
The Customer Service Representative reviews the customer's Order History and Account Notes.

The Customer Service Representative identifies that the account is in "Review Status" because the system automatically locked it when the PayPal or Amazon Payments customer allowed their order(s) to expire.
The Customer Service Representative verifies that the customer has had orders cancelled and has not paid up to three times.
If the customer is subject to the escalation policy, the Customer Service Representative confirms that the customer has updated their account with a credit card.
The Customer Service Representative unlocks the "Review Status" account to restore the customer's bidding privileges.

When an auction participant becomes subject to the escalation policy, they cannot bid again until a Customer Service Rep removes the account from Review Status; the only way for a customer to have their account removed from Review Status is by updating their account with a credit card.
They may not use PayPal or Amazon Payments again until their order cancel rate falls below 10%.

Customers cannot unlock the account themselves by paying for the orders, because the orders are automatically cancelled after 7 days (168 hours), so that this product may be returned to the inventory pool and re-auctioned.

Customer Care reps should be able to place auction customers in a “Review” status at the customer’s request or upon evidence of fraudulent or other undesirable activity; a Customer Care manager will be required to approve, via code, a permanent suspension of bidding rights (“Deactivate an Account”).
Deactivating accounts will require a supervisor's authorization code; a pop-up DIV layer will appear, asking for a supervisor's code.

If the customer is subject to the escalation policy and has not updated their account with a credit card, the account cannot be removed from Review Status and bidding privileges cannot be restored; exit: the account remains in Review Status and the customer cannot bid again until the account is updated with a credit card.

If the customer subject to the escalation policy attempts to continue using PayPal or Amazon Payments, they may not use PayPal or Amazon Payments again until their order cancel rate falls below 10%; exit: the customer must use a credit card, and the account remains subject to the escalation policy until the cancel rate condition is met.

If the customer attempts to unlock the account themselves by paying for the orders, the account cannot be unlocked that way because the orders are automatically cancelled after 7 days (168 hours) so the product may be returned to the inventory pool and re-auctioned; exit: the customer remains in Review Status unless a Customer Service Representative unlocks the account.

If evidence of fraudulent or other undesirable activity requires permanent suspension of bidding rights (“Deactivate an Account”), a Customer Care manager must approve via code; exit: permanent suspension/deactivation is not completed without the required manager approval.
The customer's account has been removed from Review Status by a Customer Service Representative.
The customer is allowed to bid again.
If the customer is subject to the escalation policy, the customer may not use PayPal or Amazon Payments again until their order cancel rate falls below 10%.
